name: Lacustrine-Corrie
description: Rock deserts and sand seas take turns under a sky like hammered brass. Between dust events the wind redraws an ancient meteor crater, patient as erosion itself.

The air carries wet iron and lichen, and sound behaves strangely: footsteps crack loud, then die without echo. At night the temperature drops fast enough to hear the rock tick as it contracts. Slow groves of photosynthetic columns migrate centimeters a season toward the light.
Around the spatial rift remnant, reality bends in small ways. Compasses sulk, clocks gain seconds, and long-stay crews develop identical tics.
Survey contracts pay double for reasons nobody writes down. Veterans read the fine print, then read the survivors.
